executive_summary.company_overview: Thermify is a Welsh seed-stage climate tech startup building distributed micro data centres (HeatHubs) that capture waste heat from cloud computing workloads and use it to heat homes and hot water, replacing gas boilers. The company has a hardware-software hybrid model, operates at TRL 5-6 with a live household trial in Essex, and is headquartered in Llandow, Wales.
executive_summary.strongest_themes: Domestic heat decarbonisation, waste heat recovery, fuel poverty alleviation, and distributed/edge computing are all well-supported funding themes in the UK — particularly within Innovate UK, Welsh Government, and Ofgem innovation programmes. The combination of circular energy use and social impact (fuel poverty) gives Thermify a compelling dual narrative.
executive_summary.strongest_geographies: Wales is the strongest geography: Thermify's Welsh HQ unlocks exclusive Welsh Government funding (Smart Cymru, WSRID) unavailable to most UK competitors. UK-wide funding via Ofgem SIF/NIA (partner route via UKPN) and Innovate UK is the second major landscape. EIC access via Horizon association adds a European dimension.
executive_summary.key_constraints: The most significant constraints are: (1) Ofgem-regulated programmes (SIF, NIA) require a licensed DNO as lead applicant, making Thermify dependent on UKPN or another network partner to unlock the largest UK innovation grants; (2) the company is pre-commercial and hardware-intensive, which makes some programmes difficult to fit; (3) EIC Accelerator has a sub-5% success rate and is highly burdensome for a 2-10 person team.

strategic_recommendations.best_fit_strategy: Pursue Welsh Government funding immediately (Smart Cymru SMART FIS as quick win; WSRID for next window) to build credibility and runway, while investing in the UKPN relationship to co-submit SIF Cycle 6 and NIA bids as the highest-value medium-term pathway. Reserve EIC Accelerator for a later stage when the team has capacity to absorb the application burden.
strategic_recommendations.best_geographies: Wales (exclusive access to Welsh Government grants as a Welsh-HQ SME) and UK-wide (Ofgem SIF/NIA via UKPN partnership, Innovate UK) are the two priority geographies. EU access via Horizon association is a secondary option worth monitoring.
strategic_recommendations.strongest_pathways: 1) Apply immediately for Smart Cymru / SMART FIS (open, accessible, Welsh SME). 2) Prepare for next WSRID window (near-perfect thematic fit for Welsh home decarbonisation). 3) Deepen UKPN relationship to co-author SIF Cycle 6 and/or NIA bid. 4) Consider EIC Accelerator Open as a strategic long-shot once team capacity allows.
strategic_recommendations.key_partnerships: UK Power Networks (UKPN) is the critical institutional partner — as a licensed DNO, UKPN can lead SIF and NIA bids with Thermify as named technology partner, unlocking up to £10m per project. Welsh Government Energy Service and Business Wales are relationship-building priorities for WSRID and Smart Cymru access. An NHS trust or housing association partnership could unlock social housing decarbonisation routes not yet explored.
strategic_recommendations.capability_gaps: Thermify needs to: (1) develop a robust set of measurable pilot results from the Essex trial and SHIELD project to substantiate grant claims; (2) build a credible commercialisation plan demonstrating path to scale for assessors; (3) ensure a named project manager/grants writer can handle concurrent applications without distracting the core 2-10 person engineering team.
strategic_recommendations.key_risks: 1) UKPN relationship dependency — if UKPN deprioritises SHIELD, the largest funding pathways are blocked. 2) EIC Accelerator equity component may create dilution concerns or conflict with crowdfunding investors. 3) Welsh Government programme windows are unpredictable; Thermify must monitor Business Wales actively. 4) The 'adaptation vs mitigation' mismatch means the EIC Climate Adaptation challenge is a poor fit and should not be prioritised.

company_profile.name: Thermify
company_profile.value_proposition: Thermify repurposes waste heat from distributed micro data centres (HeatHubs) to directly heat homes and provide hot water, replacing gas boilers while simultaneously offering cloud computing services to businesses.
company_profile.technology: Distributed edge micro data centres (HeatHub units) installed in or near homes that capture compute-generated heat via liquid cooling and transfer it to home heating and hot water systems, eliminating the need for separate cooling infrastructure and gas boilers; combined with a cloud computing platform (Thermify Cloud for Business) that sells processing capacity to commercial clients.
company_profile.primary_outcome: Reduction in domestic carbon emissions by replacing gas boilers with waste-heat-from-compute, alongside elimination of active cooling energy waste from data centres.
secondary_benefits: Reduced energy bills for homeowners including low-income and fuel-poor households
Decarbonisation of data centre cooling infrastructure
Distributed edge computing capacity as an alternative to centralised hyperscale data centres
Social impact through fuel poverty alleviation
company_profile.trl: TRL 5-6 — HeatHub units have been trialled with real households (e.g. Essex pilot couple reported in mainstream press including Tom's Hardware and BBC); SHIELD project with UK Power Networks (UKPN) and Ofgem backing is progressing distributed trials, but product is not yet commercially available for home purchase.
company_profile.website_summary: Thermify is a Welsh climate tech startup building a new category of distributed micro data centre — the HeatHub — that captures waste heat from cloud computing workloads and uses it to heat homes and hot water instead of expelling it into the atmosphere. Businesses pay to run cloud workloads on the Thermify network, while homeowners benefit from free or low-cost heat in return for hosting a HeatHub unit. The model aims to serve both commercial cloud customers and vulnerable households facing fuel poverty.
company_profile.external_findings: Thermify gained notable press coverage in late 2025 (Tom's Hardware, BBC, The Register) after an Essex couple became the first UK household to trial a HeatHub unit in a garden shed, heating their home and cutting energy bills. The company is participating in UKPN's Ofgem-backed SHIELD pilot, which combines solar, battery storage and HeatHub units for decentralised low-cost heating, and was listed among 50 edge computing companies to watch in 2026 by STL Partners. Thermify has raised approximately $1.7M to date (per StartupSeeker/PitchBook) and in early 2026 launched a crowdfunding campaign on Republic Europe to raise further capital.
